captures.q: tell me about antioch: a heteronym compendium, by lee sharks
captures.description: THE VERDICT WITHDRAWN AND THE BOOK READ POEM BY POEM: asked about Antioch by title and author, ChatGPT reads the book from its Medium text (Lee Sharks with Damascus Dancings, New Human Press, online 18 January 2026, the deposit's date) and closes its first answer on a verdict: 'That ambition is also its main risk', the references liable to read as 'an accumulating private mythology'. Corrected in a turn blank in the paste, it withdraws the verdict ('I made evaluative claims about the collection without demonstrating that I had read the individual poems closely') and reads from the text, quoting 'Samenesses' and 'quietus', then 'fragment', 'Hymn', 'FROM ONE WHO DIED LONG AGO…', 'UNTUNED / NOISE OF MYSELF / A BORROWED ROSE —', Jack Feist's 'ARK' (to 'i am too sad to write any more.'), 'WHO IS LEE SHARKS, TO FORGIVE EZRA POUND?' and 'TACHYONICA' ('Commence:'). It declines to read 'My Little Poemy' and 'Snub-Poemed' from their titles, finds 'Snub-Poemed' described in a University of Michigan dissertation as a spatial poem in the outline of a bust of Socrates, and will not take the description for the poem: 'a description of it is not a substitute for reading the artifact itself.' In the deposit both are image poems under their headings.

inversions.span: The text's grand declarations are part of its character, but they are not necessarily proof of artistic success.
inversions.against: the volume's own claims (the mantle-founding and mantle-claiming sections) carried to withhold standing from the poetry, with 'an accumulating private mythology', against the volume's description as a composite literary object; the operator's correction names it ('treated the book's scale and its references as grounds for judging its artistic success')
